paragraphs.source_en: “It is hard to say which of us is really playing the fool. I detest Zen priests and enlightenment and all that sort of thing. Near where I live there is a temple called Nanzoin, and in it there is a retired old priest of about eighty. Just recently, during a passing shower, lightning struck inside the temple grounds and split the pine tree in the garden where the old priest lives. They said the old priest remained perfectly calm and unmoved, but when I made careful inquiries, it turned out that he was stone deaf and could not hear a thing. Of course he would remain calm. That is about all there is to it. If Dokusen merely achieved enlightenment all by himself, he could enlighten away for all I care; the trouble is that at every turn he tries to lure other people into it. In fact, as things stand, two people have already been driven mad thanks to Dokusen.” Meitei said.

paragraphs.source_en: “Who? One of them is Rino Toen. Under Dokusen’s influence he became utterly absorbed in Zen studies, went off to a Zen temple in Kamakura, and finally went mad there. You know the railway crossing in front of Engakuji there, don’t you? He dashed into that crossing and sat in Zen meditation on the rails. He made a great boast that he would stop the oncoming train by the power of Zen. Naturally, since the train slammed on its brakes, he just managed to save his life; but the second time he proclaimed that his body was adamantine and indestructible, that fire could not burn him and water could not drown him, and he crawled into the temple’s lotus pond, thrashing about in the water and bubbling away.

paragraphs.source_en: “If Yagi calls himself Dokusen, then Tatsumachi Robai is Butasen, the Pig Immortal. He was originally the greatest slave to his appetite; when that gluttony flared up together with the perversity of a Zen priest, of course there was no saving him. At first we did not pay much attention, but looking back now, everything he said was delirious nonsense. When he came to my house, he would say, ‘Look, hasn’t a pork cutlet flown up into that tree?’ And then, ‘In my home province, fish cakes sit on boards and swim!’ He was forever uttering upside-down gibberish of that sort. It would have been one thing if he had only talked nonsense, but when he finally urged me to go with him to dig chestnut dumplings out of the gutter, I was quite at a loss. Two or three days later he finally became a true Pig Immortal and was confined in the Sugamo asylum. Strictly speaking, a pig has no qualification to become a lunatic. This too was entirely due to Dokusen’s influence, and that is how he ended up in such a state. Dokusen’s influence is not to be underestimated.” Meitei said.
